messages.subject: Re: Regarding assembly support
parts: i) Following my previous question, is there no use of assembly, it is merely a string that needs to provide for user's information?
This is for the user and some of the functions, for example the package will not let you merge methylRaw objects if they have different assembly strings.

ii) Regarding annotation, there is no annotation information is given in the refseq.hg18.bed.txt in any column. Then how is methylKitR able to decide the annotation boundaries (e.g. exons, introns, promoters etc) on the basis of co-ordinates. Does it take assembly into consideration at this step?

Read about the BED format description. BED12 format has that information. As a user you have to make sure you use the CpG methylation information from the same assembly as the BED file. Most bed files will not have an assembly information embedded in the file, that's why we can't check if the annotation assembly and methylKit object assembly matches or not.

Shalu

in any case, I think you don't have enough memory for the task at hand. It takes time and memory to read large files.

1. Filter the CpGs that have coverage below 10X from the files
2. if 1 is not enough, you should be able to split the files based on their chromosome, it is an  awk one liner. see here:http://seqanswers.com/forums/showthread.php?t=8115

then, in a for loop, read the files for each chromosome and use unite() to merge them into one table per chromosome, append each methylBase object to a result list.
After you exit the loop you can try to merge the data in the list. I can help you in more detail if you can get to that stage. But try the first suggestion.

best,
Altuna

The idea is based on removing principal components that corresponds to a batch effect and reconstructing the data. It is a very crude way of dealing with the problem but it might work, there are other alternatives such as SVA (BioC package)

you have to use first assocComp() to find components associated with your known batches, and then use removeComp() to remove the components associated with batches. see the examples at help pages of those functions.

We are working on dealing with covariates such as known batch effects in other ways. It will hopefully available soon to test as an external script.

I don't know if UCSC maps one-to-one with ensemble? Same number of lines doesn't not prove mapping is one-to-one. You also have repeating coordinates in your file, I don't think your file contains the same information as the methylKit promoter files. In methylKit file, there is one promoter per unique TSS. There is an argument you can change in read.transcript.features() so that you get one promoter for each transcript, but in that case you will have redundant locations, transcript isoforms having the same TSS will have the same promoter coordinates. see the help page for that function.

Since the last e-mail you are making the same mistake when calculating the promoter coordinates. You can easily verify what you are doing is correct by pasting your coordinates to UCSC browser (as many as you can). If you do that, you will see some of your promoter coordinates doesn't make sense.

here is a coordinate from your file: chr1 4280825 4281925
What you call promoter in that location is the 3' end of the gene, and that is not the promoter but a region around transcription end. And, I think that explains most of the discrepancy. 

Here is the UCSC url:
http://genome-euro.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?db=mm9&position=chr1%3A4280826-4281925&hgsid=197592283_4LZ6nD6R3JhEWLCPr68io8aQYgCm

for the chrM, promoter start coordinate is minus because probably the TSS is close to the start of the chromosome. It shouldn't cause a problem when summarizing the methylation values, you just have to correct for it later on.

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: Regarding assembly support
parts:
Hi Altuna,

Is it possible to perform annotation of DMRs (bed: chr:start:end) by methylKit? How can I do this?

I have those DMRs from other sources and I want to see the annotation. I was performing it using methylkit by:
gene.obj=read.transcript.features("/users/GD/resource/mouse/mm9/annotation/genes/UCSC_annotation.bed", down.flank=100)
diffAnn=annotate.WithGenicParts(myDiff25p,gene.obj)

where myDiff25p is a methyKit object. So I wonder if I can convert the bed file of DMRs into this object to perform annotation or any other method?
Could you please suggest?

I would highly appreciate your quick reply,

Thanks!
Shalu

On Wed, Jul 16, 2014 at 1:24 PM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
countOverlaps() takes into account the strand if strand information is given as either  "-" or "+". If you have the locations of CpG dinucleotides in the cpg_object it should return the counts of overlapping CpG dinucleotides per region in cluster.obj. You can experiment with those functions giving small pieces of input objects where you know what the correct answer is.

I can not tell you if you are doing something correctly or not, you are sending tiny bit of your code without any data but it seems to be OK (but I might be wrong as there is not enough information)

Best,
Altuna




On Mon, Jul 14, 2014 at 6:52 PM, shalu jhanwar <shalu.j...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Altuna,

Thank you for your kind reply. It worked and now I can understand the direction.
Also I want to know that how many CpGs are clustered within the promoter boundaries. As suggested by you, I coerce methylBase object to GRanges like:
 grange_object<-as(cluster.meth.myData,"GRanges") but I don't know how to perform countOverlap on it.

When I saw the usage, countOverlap needs two GRanges objects and then it will give a interger output. So I performed like below:
cluster.obj=GRanges(seqnames=bed$V1,ranges=IRanges(start=bed$V2, end=bed$V3),strand=bed$V6)
 cpg_obj<-GRanges(seqnames=CpG_bed$V1,ranges=IRanges(start=CpG_bed$V2, end=CpG_bed$V3),strand=CpG_bed$V6)
countOverlaps(cluster.obj, cpg_obj)

Also, it is not taking strand information into consideration while giving overlap. Moreover, after this output, still I am not sure what no. of CpGs are clustered in methylBase object.

Can you please let me know the way to do this correctly as this question is important in my analysis ? I would highly appreciate your reply,

Thanks!

Shalu

Thanks for your quick reply.

I would highly appreciate it.

Shalu

Best,
Altuna

Hypomethylated: means Methylation S1 > S2

Shalu
